newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says asthma drug to be key product.
newsitem.headline: Astra says asthma drug to be key product.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra AB said on Monday its asthma treatment Oxis Turbuhaler was one of the company's biggest launches in recent years and could become its third most important drug.
"This is probably Astra's biggest launch since Losec," Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters.
Astra said earlier on Monday that it had won its first approval for its asthma inhaler, the Oxis Turbuhaler, and the drug would be launched in Sweden early 1997.
It also said it expected to gain pan-European approval for the drug in 1997 and the product would be available in the United States and Japan in a few years.
Ternby said the drug could become the company's largest seller after anti-ulcer drug Losec and respiratory drug Pulmicort.
Sales of Pulmicort totalled 4.34 billion crowns in 1995 and sales of the company's fourth largest selling drug, Seloken, totalled 2.43 billion crowns last year.
Astra said Oxis Turbuhaler was a long-acting bronchodilator.
"In 1995 the inhaled bronchodilator market was worth 13.6 billion crowns. The value of this market for the year 2000 is forecast to be 21 billion crowns," it said in a statement.
"Long-acting inhaled bronchodilators will probably represent 40 percent of these sales."
Astra said the drug combined the drug formoterol and Astra's inhaler system, the Turbuhaler.
"Formoterol has advantages over existing long acting bronchodilators such as salmeterol, with a much faster onset of action," it said.
The drug works for 12 hours and begins working 15 to 30 seconds after inhaling. Rival products begin working only after 15 to 30 minutes, Ternby said.
